assumptions: Bilateral and repetition-based, with no external load beyond bodyweight.
Foot height (floor or low box) changes load but not the joint actions, so it is not modeled.
Torso stays close and upright to the bench; the concentric phase is the push back up to the start.
Shoulder flexion back toward neutral is an assist action that helps raise the torso.
Hips stay roughly in the same position and the knees stay extended, so legs add no prime movers.
classification_reasons: Bodyweight bench dip with both hands gripping the bench edge behind the torso, a clear elbow-extension push-up phase, and a fixed hand support.
The two frames agree with the text: arms extended at the top, elbows flexed with the torso lowered at the bottom.
All joint actions and stabilization demands are in the schema vocabulary.
